also: I don’t know what he looks like

evidence: Plaut. Rud. 4.4.111: Quā faciē sunt? (Lewis & Short), s.v. faciēs
Traupman p. 102: quā sit faciē, nesciō
terms.comment: The look of a person or thing is an ablative of quality: quā faciē, “of what appearance”; in an indirect question the verb goes into the subjunctive: quā sit faciē, nesciō.

phrases.english: I don’t know what he looks like.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 102, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
